quick: Typically 100 to 300 mg per 5 to 10 mL dose in combination syrups, three to four times daily
summary: Ammonium chloride is used in Indian cough syrups as an expectorant (claimed to increase bronchial secretion by gastric reflex irritation). It is also a systemic acidifying agent. Evidence for benefit in cough is weak.
indications: Productive cough, as an expectorant in combination syrups
Historically: metabolic alkalosis and urinary acidification (specialist use)

dosage.d: Typically 100 to 300 mg per 5 to 10 mL dose in combination syrups, three to four times daily

admin: Use only as the finished product directs
moa: Irritates the gastric mucosa, reflexly increasing respiratory tract secretion. Absorbed ammonium is converted to urea in the liver, releasing hydrogen and chloride ions (acidifying effect).
preg: Safety not established; use only if clearly needed
lact: Safety not established; weigh benefit against unknown risk
hepatic: Avoid in hepatic impairment: risk of hyperammonaemia

moderate: Increases renal excretion of basic drugs (amphetamines, some opioids) and reduces that of acidic drugs, through urine acidification

counsel: Use exactly as the pack directs
Stop and seek care for rash, swelling or breathing difficulty
missed: Take it when remembered unless the next dose is due; do not double up.
overdose: No specific antidote. Supportive and symptomatic care.
